cells.tense: The pen is in your hand and the room is open around you.
cells.act: dream the next step and take it
cells.ask: Picture a step you haven't tried, small enough to do badly, and do it this week. Nothing needs to come of it.
cells.core:
You can hold a fire for other people — keep them going, keep the light steady, and not burn down while you do it. That part is working. And the ground around you has opened up: something that couldn't hold has fallen away and the way forward is wider than it was. The two are feeding each other. You can stand in the open and warm the next thing without grabbing it or doubting it.

The tender part is imagining what hasn't happened yet. Picture a step you haven't tried, small enough that doing it badly still counts, and take it. Then keep doing what you don't stop doing — give the next person a reason to keep going, and mean it. Watch whether the fire stays lit when your own hands are the ones feeding it.
cells.sheetLine: The ground is open and you can walk into it.
cells.verb: tend the fire and keep going
cells.place: in the clearing the collapse leaves

cells.tense: You're braced for the next wall to fall, though this one is already down.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: Before you say the true thing to someone, check once what they can hear right now. Keep the truth, change the delivery. A hard thing said gently still counts.
cells.core:
Where you carry the fire for others, you're carrying it for a blow you've already seen coming. So you're three moves ahead — explaining, hardening, building backstops for a wall that's already down. The energy is still for them. It just isn't in this room anymore.

The refit is the same steadiness turned around. Look at what you're shielding someone from before you shield them. One sentence, tested against what they can take right now, saves you the pushing. The wall that fell was not one worth keeping. Say the thing out loud, gently, and see whether the sky is still up there. It is, and you can stop bracing against it.
cells.sheetLine: You're braced for a wall that's already down.
cells.verb: tend the fire and keep going
cells.place: in the clearing the collapse leaves

cells.tense: The clearing opened and you're still standing at the doorway that was there before.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Clear one finished thing out of the room — the superseded draft, the ended plan, the object kept for a reason that's gone. Put it out, and bring nothing in.
cells.core:
Somewhere along the way the fire stopped being tended. Not through cruelty — the structure came down and you didn't quite move past the doorway. The care is still in your hands. It isn't reaching the open air yet, and the ground out there stays cold while you stand here.

You don't have to feel moved to move the furniture. Take one finished thing out this week: the draft that's been superseded, the plan that ended, the object you kept because it used to matter. Feel it as you do it, and notice what's left standing when it's gone. What remains after a clearing is still warm. The work was not to earn a direction — it was to stop heating a space with nothing growing in it.
cells.sheetLine: Let one finished thing out and the room stays warm.
cells.verb: tend the fire and keep going

cells.tense: The pen has been down in a room you've been writing in the whole time.
cells.act: move the structure one real inch
cells.ask: Take one slow push this week on the change already underway — one notch, one step, no burst. Then note what you moved so it exists outside you.
cells.core:
You talk about the clearing as something that happened to you — the structure fell and you were standing there. Maybe so. But the small, quiet moves you were making before it came down are still yours, and nobody has asked you about them, so they've been filed under circumstance.

Here is what circumstance doesn't do. Take one slow push this week on the change already underway: one notch, one step, no burst of effort. Then put a note somewhere that the inch moved, so it exists outside your head. It's the same inch you'd have moved anyway, except now your name is on it, and the next inch is easier when the last one is on the record.
cells.sheetLine: The inch you moved was yours.
cells.verb: tend the fire and keep going

attempts.check: The record never says the person keeps the old thing; it says the structure couldn't hold. So 'what you already know is finished' presses past what's drawn. A reader could fairly say the clearing came from outside them, not from them. The asks survive that: each is a small act in the person's own hands whether or not my read of them is right. And the sentence that serves me more than them is any line casting the clearing as dramatic — cut from every core.
